translation: The Du governs the yang at the back of the body, while the Ren and the Chong govern the yin at the front of the body — spoken of in terms of north and south. The Dai vessel binds the various vessels transversely — spoken of in terms of the six directions (liuhe). For this reason, if a physician knows the eight vessels, then the great purport of the twelve primary channels and the fifteen connecting vessels is attained.
